newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish military attacks Islamists over sackings.
newsitem.headline: Turkish military attacks Islamists over sackings.

text.p: Turkey's influential military criticised Islamist MPs and the pro-Islam press for their opposition to the sacking of 58 men thrown out of the armed forces for Islamist tendencies.
"Certain press organs and their supporters will definitely not be permitted to erode the Turkish armed forces," the secularist Sabah daily on Friday quoted a senior military official as saying.
The small Islamist press and some members of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party have criticised the army for the sackings earlier this week.

Erbakan himself has also been taken to task in the normally supportive Islamist press for approving the cleanout at a military council meeting earlier this week. Eleven other servicemen were discharged for involvement in politics.

Anti-Islamist comments from unnamed military officials appeared in other major newspapers. A high-ranking officer told the Milliyet daily that the staunchly secularist army would not tolerate Islamist or any other political movements in the ranks.
"Introducing political and ideological views into the Turkish armed forces would create differences of opinion from top to bottom," the officer said.
Erbakan, in coalition with a secularist party, has been ineffective in bringing Islamist policies to bear in areas of public life regarded by the generals as within their remit.
He has gone back on promises to scrap a military deal with Israel and throw out a U.S.-led air force that patrols northern Iraq from a base in Turkey.
